note: Missing the subject. Without `did` there is nothing to update.
A partial service set. `services` replaces the whole set, so both `mediator` and `tsp` must be stated; a set that leaves one out would silently withdraw a transport the caller never mentioned.
The precondition in the webvh form. A did:webs version is `<sequence number>:<SAID>`; `3-Qm…` is a did:webvh versionId, and accepting it would compare against nothing.
A caller-chosen key agreement key. The VTA derives it; the closed schema refuses a key the caller supplies.
A signing-key change smuggled into an update. Keys change only through rotate-keys, and an unknown member is refused rather than ignored.
The DID is not a did:webs DID. This family manages no other method.
